speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear you're feeling this way. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how much weight you've lost and over what period of time? Also, have you noticed any night sweats or fevers recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient reports a 6-month history of fatigue and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg (11 lb) despite maintaining a good appetite. He denies any recent changes in his diet or physical activity. He takes no medications and does not smoke or use illicit drugs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and these constitutional symptoms, have you noticed any persistent cough, shortness of breath, or bone pain? Also, have you experienced any changes in bowel habits or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have 5 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, Good appetite. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unusual, as cellulitis typically presents with localized redness, warmth, and swelling rather than systemic fatigue and significant weight loss. Can you describe exactly where you felt the skin infection and what the skin looked like? Additionally, have you noticed any night sweats, fevers, or lymph node enlargement elsewhere?

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work is completely normal, which makes an active infection like cellulitis very unlikely given your systemic symptoms. Since you have a good appetite but are still losing weight and feel fatigued, where specifically did the previous doctor find the skin infection, and have you noticed any enlarged lumps under your arms or in your neck?
